project.description:
A technique host for a target somebody else owns and presents: an ordered RenderTechnique list composited into a SampledColorTarget, rather than into a window and swapchain of the engine's own.
It exists because the stack has two places a frame is composited and the SPI was wired to one of them. vexelray-engine owns a window, a swapchain and a frame loop, which is right for an application whose whole surface is the scene; an application whose scene is a *region* of a GUI window gets its target from the host (GuiApp.viewport) and presents by being sampled. Before this module those applications could not use a technique at all -- they drove vexelray-vulkan by hand, one pipeline each, and the two that did drifted apart.
Why its own module rather than a class in vexelray-engine-vulkan-api: that module is the technique contract and nothing else (D18), and this is a concrete runtime. Why not in vexelray-engine: depending on it would drag a window, a swapchain, a frame loop and a ServiceLoader-resolved EngineProvider into an application that wanted none of them, which is the reachability-metadata cost a native-image host pays for a facade it never calls. RenderTechnique's own javadoc anticipates exactly this module -- "a second Vulkan runtime -- an offscreen one for tests, a runtime embedding into somebody else's swapchain -- could not have served the techniques that already exist. As an interface in a module of its own, it can."
